| 2026-08-29 | src/components/Game/ascendant-bar/HooksBlock.tsx | Chips gained a `sheetId`, set by a per-chip probe through `attachmentDetailFromNode`; `Chip` takes `onOpen` only when a destination resolved, and answers Space as well as Enter | THR-1330. Law 1 reached these chips only because THR-1307 made them render at all. The probe is the sheet's own classifier rather than a per-row rule, so the bar cannot disagree with `AttachmentDetailView` about what has a page: a `condition` links, a `clue` does not, and an authored `category: 'mark'` — which buckets into Conditions but is not an attachment subcategory — fails open instead of getting Law 21's dead link that looks live. No image on any kind, on THR-1120's standing ruling that `EntityVisualKind` excludes `attachment`; measured 0 of 214 attachment templates carry `props.image`, so a tile would be the fallback glyph on every chip and would need a borrowed kind to get there (Law 3). |
| 2026-08-29 | src/components/Game/ascendant-bar/styles.module.css | `.chip` no longer sets `cursor: pointer`; `Chip` sets it inline from whether it resolved a destination | THR-1330. THR-1307 removed the `role`/`tabIndex` half of the false advertisement and left the cursor behind, so every inert chip still claimed to be clickable in the channel the player reads *before* committing to the click. |
| 2026-08-29 | src/components/Game/ascendant-bar/AscendantBar.tsx, src/components/Game/GameView.tsx | `onOpenAttachment` threaded to `HooksBlock`, wired to the existing `setAttachmentSheetId` | THR-1330. Deliberately the same setter the aftermath consequence chip uses: the condition granted at the end of an encounter and the condition sitting on the bar afterwards open one sheet, not two that could drift (Law 3). `attachmentSheetId` is also what `GameView` reports to `__DEBUG.getOpenModals()` as `AttachmentDetailView`, so the chip's destination is observable from the debug bridge. |
| 2026-08-29 | src/components/Game/ascendant-bar/__tests__/hooksBlockLink.test.tsx, .../hooksBlockComposedBar.test.tsx | Two render suites — the block, and the composed bar | THR-1330. `Browser-verify substitution: jsdom-render — unattended run, no startable dev server`. | 2026-08-29 | Docs/impediments.md | Impediment #940 logged — two armed PRs stalled `DIRTY` for 7.6 h and 4.6 h, one of them blocked a second independent way | `tb-opus-pickup` hourly run. PRs #1714 (THR-1322) and #1717 (THR-1344) were both pure closeout-doc conflicts that `git merge origin/main` settled in one command each via the union driver, yet both had held their In-Dev slots overnight: a conflicted PR is never built, so no required check runs, auto-merge stays armed and never fires, and every surface except `mergeStateStatus` reads as shipped. #1717 also carried a red required check — two independent blockers, so a conflict-only repair would have left it unmergeable and re-reporting next hour under a different verdict (the #466 shape). The durable note: `check:armed-prs` already emits the right verdict hourly — what was missing is a run willing to spend its slot on the verdict rather than on a fresh claim. |
| 2026-08-28 | src/engine/tradeRoute.ts | `TRADE_ROUTE_FOUNDING_GRACE_WINDOW` (36) added, plus the `isRouteUnderFoundersGrace` predicate | THR-1320. `createTradeRoute` is the sole minter of `trades_with` and mints at `volume: 1`; `TRADE_ROUTE_DECAY_RATE` is also 1; nothing in the strategic path refreshes `lastTraded` (only the divine trade verbs do). So a route founded by a six-tick undertaking went stale at +6 and was removed — 0 routes standing at tick 150 on seeds 42 and 99. Sized to outlast the counter-play's detect-and-complete cycle (`UNDERTAKING_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_TICKS` 6 + the blockade's `projectDuration` 4), not picked round. A **window, not an exemption**: an immortal held route would accumulate all run and inflate prosperity map-wide. Gated on `establishedBy`, so weather still decays on inactivity alone. |
| 2026-08-28 | src/engine/tradeRoute.ts | `readTradeRouteProps` now reads the birth tick from `establishedTick`, keeping `established` as a legacy fallback; `establishedBy` added to the read shape | THR-1320. Every writer in the tree stamps `establishedTick`; the reader looked only at `established`, which no writer sets — so it resolved to its `0` default on **every route that has ever existed**. Load-bearing in one place (`totalTicksActive` on the dissolved trace, which reported the absolute tick as a lifetime), and it would have silently defeated a grace window keyed on founding tick. |
| 2026-08-28 | src/engine/phaseTradeRouteDecay.ts | Founder's-grace skip added ahead of the staleness test | THR-1320. | 2026-08-24 | `src/data/content-eval/nudgeAuthoringConstants.ts`, `src/engine/__tests__/nudgeModel.test.ts` | THR-831: verdict on `NUDGE_OFF_REACH_MAX_DIFFICULTY = 0.45` — **it stands, unchanged**, and the retune option the ticket offered is arithmetically backwards. Boundary now pinned in both directions (+2 tests): the whole off-reach cohort clearing at a full non-trait hand with probabilities as literals, plus the monotonicity of the difficulty term and the 0.6192 crossover. | The constant's justification claimed an off-reach `notable` stays floored *through the whole hand* at 0.45, citing +0.37 — one ascendant's sphere-gated subset, not the hand's ceiling (THR-827). At the reachable +0.55 the cohort clears. But `p = capability − difficulty + modifiers` puts difficulty on the **same side as the floor**: *lowering* the ceiling makes hands clear more easily, never less, and keeping the strongest member pinned against 0.55 would mean **raising** it to 0.6192 — into `severe`, the band the rule exists to keep open-draw content out of. So the ceiling's direction was always right and only its rationale was wrong. The game-feel answer falls out of the same arithmetic: a god with essence across many spheres lifting an off-reach mortal off the floor is what broad sphere access buys, and a ceiling tuned to prevent it would make broad access buy nothing — the decorative-hand failure in its other form. Pinning only the floored side is *how* the rationale came to claim more than it had measured. |

| 2026-07-21 | .github/workflows/ci.yml, scripts/check-typecheck-ratchet.ts (new), typecheck-baseline.json (new), package.json, CLAUDE.md, Docs/project-status.md, Docs/project-history.md | THR-693: CI's `Typecheck` step ran `npx tsc --noEmit`, which is a **no-op** here — root `tsconfig.json` sets `files: []`, so it exited 0 unconditionally. The required `Test · Typecheck · Build` check asserted a type gate in its name while containing none; THR-686 purged that claim from six *documents* but never touched the workflow, so the theater outlived its own retraction. Shipped option (b), the **ratchet**: `npm run check:typecheck` runs `tsc -b --force --pretty false`, counts diagnostics, compares against the committed `typecheck-baseline.json` (**3529** errors across 763 files, independently cross-checked by grep), and fails **only on an increase**. Bare `tsc -b` was explicitly rejected per the handoff — it turns the required check red on arrival and blocks every PR, trading a gate that cannot fail for one that cannot pass. Three flags are load-bearing and documented as such in the script header: `--force` (without it `tsc -b` is incremental and reports nothing against a warm `.tsbuildinfo` — a false pass worse than the no-op it replaces), `--pretty false` (pins the single-line diagnostic format the parser depends on; the TTY format silently scores as 0 errors), and an unverifiable-run guard (a tsc failure producing no parseable diagnostics exits non-zero rather than reading as "0 errors"). The gate is the **total only**; a per-file map is carried purely to make failures actionable — "3530 > 3529" is unactionable against a 3529-error baseline — and per-file drift alone never fails, so refactors that merely move errors between files generate no baseline churn. | Proven in both directions before commit, because a gate not demonstrated to fail is the same theater in a new costume: unchanged tree → `OK — 3529, unchanged`; one injected error → `FAIL — 3529 → 3530 (+1)`, exit 1, naming `src/engine/traceBuffer.ts: 3 → 4`. The failure message states that the ~3529 baseline is pre-existing (THR-489) and *not the executor's to fix*, because the likeliest failure mode of a ratchet on a deeply red baseline is an agent reading a FAIL as "fix 3529 errors" and either burning a run or working around the gate. A count-below-baseline run passes and *asks* for a refresh rather than auto-writing one — CI cannot commit, and silently lowering the floor from a machine that cannot record why would make the baseline untraceable. CLAUDE.md's claim that CI "runs `tsc -b`" was false in the other direction too and is corrected to describe the ratchet, with the local command being the identical one, so a local pass now genuinely predicts CI. |
